questions.questionHTML:
Match the statement/s from column 1 with column 2 and find which of the following pairs of statements given in the options make/s contextually and grammatically correct sense.

Column IColumn II
A. Wearing several layers, for instance, enables you to take offD. This year the price rise was a tad bit on the higher side
B. The elevated inflation levels robbed peopleE. You to customise your attire for the task at hand
C. While it is not unusual for egg prices to increase in the winterF. Of their purchasing power and worsened India's trade deficit
questions.explanationHTML:
Correct Answer: c) Both B-F and C-D

Explanation:
• B-F: "The elevated inflation levels robbed people of their purchasing power and worsened India's trade deficit" is grammatically and contextually sound ('robbed someone of something').
• C-D: "While it is not unusual for egg prices to increase in the winter, this year the price rise was a tad bit on the higher side" forms a coherent contrast.
• A-E is grammatically incorrect because 'enables you to take off you to customise' repeats the object pronoun.

questions.questionHTML:
Match the statement/s from column 1 with column 2 and find which of the following pairs of statements given in the options make/s sense contextually and grammatically.

Column 1Column 2
A. The train departed earlier than expected and soD. Peak of summer and the sunlight is blinding at these times.
B. The snake is bred in captivity and that is whyE. It is used to its own company and dislikes other snakes.
C. The sun is shining a bit extra bright today as it is theF. Passengers were running across the platform to catch the train.
questions.explanationHTML:
Correct Answer: c) All A-F, B-E & C-D

Explanation:
• A-F: "The train departed earlier than expected and so passengers were running across the platform to catch the train."
• B-E: "The snake is bred in captivity and that is why it is used to its own company and dislikes other snakes."
• C-D: "The sun is shining a bit extra bright today as it is the peak of summer and the sunlight is blinding at these times."
All three pairs form contextually and grammatically meaningful sentences.

Directions :Given below is a set of six sentences, which when properly sequenced, form a coherent paragraph. Arrange the sentences in the correct sequence, and answer the questions that follow.

A. This patch was formed by the North Pacific Subtropical Gyre, a system of circulating ocean currents that pulls debris into its centre.

B. The concentration of plastic poses a significant threat to marine life, as animals can mistake it for food or become entangled in larger pieces.

C. The Great Pacific Garbage Patch is a vast accumulation of marine debris located in the central North Pacific Ocean, often described as a floating island of trash.

D. Addressing this environmental issue is incredibly challenging due to the patch's massive size and its remote location in international waters.

E. It is not a solid mass but is primarily composed of microplastics, which are tiny plastic particles resulting from the breakdown of larger plastic items.

F. The gyre's slow, circular motion traps the debris, preventing it from escaping and allowing it to concentrate over a very large area.
questions.questionHTML: Which of the following will be the FIRST sentence after rearrangement?
questions.explanationHTML:
Correct Answer: b) C

Explanation (Parajumble Sequence: C - E - A - F - B - D):
• C is the opening sentence as it introduces the central subject: "The Great Pacific Garbage Patch is a vast accumulation of marine debris..."
• E follows C by clarifying the "floating island of trash" metaphor: "It is not a solid mass but is primarily composed of microplastics..."
• A explains how "This patch was formed by the North Pacific Subtropical Gyre..."
• F elaborates on "The gyre's slow, circular motion traps the debris... allowing it to concentrate..."
• B links "The concentration of plastic poses a significant threat to marine life..."
• D concludes with the challenge of addressing this environmental issue.

In the following question, a sentence is given with four words marked as (A), (B), (C), and (D). These words may or may not be placed at the right places. Four options with different arrangements of these words are given. Mark the option with the correct rearrangement as the answer. If no change is required, mark 'No rearrangement required' as your answer.

The study of 135 likely(A) girls found the female teenagers who were most appearance(B) to report depressive symptoms when comparing their adolescent(C) to others were those who reported(D) higher levels of "self-critical perfectionism".
questions.explanationHTML:
Correct Answer: d) CABD

Explanation:
• Position 1 requires an adjective modifying "girls" → adolescent (C).
• Position 2 requires an adjective after "most" → likely (A) ("most likely to report").
• Position 3 requires a noun after "comparing their" → appearance (B).
• Position 4 remains reported (D).
Correct rearrangement: CABD.

Hence, CABD is the correct sequence.

Directions : In the following passage, some of the words have been left out and replaced with blanks represented by letters. First, read the passage and try to understand what it is about. Then fill in the blanks as per the questions given.

One major way the brain and heart communicate is through the autonomic nervous system. Think of the autonomic nervous system as a network of paths that ___(A)___ different brain areas to many bodily organs. It helps regulate processes that you are not generally aware of, like your heartbeat or breathing, or how fast the food you eat is digested. The connections between the autonomic nervous system and the organs can be ___(B)___ into two parts: sympathetic and parasympathetic. The sympathetic nervous system mostly pitches in during times of ___(C)___ or excitement, like if you ever need to run away from a dangerous animal, or when you feel motivated. The parasympathetic nervous system promotes relaxation of the body and supports vital functions like digestion. Thinking in terms of the body's band, the way the brain and heart communicate through the autonomic nervous system is like the singer and drummer silently communicating with gestures and ___(D)___ expressions. If the singer delivers the lyrics with more urgency, the drummer needs to match the intensity, similar to how the brain's sympathetic signaling can increase the heart rate. A gentler, more relaxed style of singing ___(E)___ cues the drummer to slow down, just as parasympathetic activity slows the heartbeat.
questions.questionHTML: Which of the following is the most appropriate option to fill the blank (A)?
questions.explanationHTML:
Correct Answer: a) connects

Explanation:
The antecedent of "that" is "a network" (singular), so it requires the singular present-tense verb "connects" ("a network of paths that connects different brain areas to many bodily organs").

questions.passageHTML:
Directions : Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

For much of the late twentieth century, Chinese manufacturing was associated primarily with low-cost, low-durability goods designed to meet mass demand in price-sensitive markets. These products were often dismissed in advanced economies as functional but inferior substitutes, suitable mainly where affordability outweighed performance. Over time, however, this perception has become increasingly outdated. Chinese firms have steadily moved beyond cost-led competitiveness to invest in research, design, and systems integration, allowing them to compete in segments once dominated by Western and Japanese manufacturers.

This transformation has been driven by a deliberate alignment of industrial policy, scale advantages, and technological learning. Rather than relying solely on imitation, firms have absorbed global knowledge while adapting it to domestic conditions, producing innovations that are incremental yet cumulative. As a result, Chinese products now incorporate advanced software, data-driven optimisation, and integrated supply chains that reduce production cycles and improve reliability. The emphasis has shifted from merely producing cheaper alternatives to delivering products that combine affordability with technical sophistication.

The implications of this shift extend beyond consumer markets into strategic sectors such as renewable energy, telecommunications, and advanced manufacturing. Countries long regarded as technological leaders increasingly recognise that China is not only catching up but, in some domains, setting benchmarks. Even economies like Germany, traditionally confident in their engineering depth, express concern about the speed and coordination with which Chinese firms translate research into scalable output. This unease is not rooted solely in price competition but in the possibility that established innovation hierarchies may be reconfigured.

Western responses to this development reveal an underlying tension. On the one hand, collaboration with Chinese suppliers remains economically attractive due to efficiency gains and integrated production networks. On the other, policymakers and industries worry about dependency, standards control, and long-term competitiveness. The debate is therefore less about whether Chinese products have improved and more about how global systems should adapt to a landscape in which technological leadership is no longer geographically concentrated. Understanding this evolution requires moving beyond outdated stereotypes and acknowledging the structural capabilities that now underpin Chinese manufacturing.
questions.questionHTML: Which of the following statements is FALSE according to the passage?

options.html: Chinese manufacturing was earlier perceived as prioritising affordability over performance.
options.text: Chinese manufacturing was earlier perceived as prioritising affordability over performance.

options.html: Chinese firms have completely abandoned cost competitiveness in favour of premium pricing.
options.text: Chinese firms have completely abandoned cost competitiveness in favour of premium pricing.

options.html: Technological learning and policy alignment have contributed to China's manufacturing shift.
options.text: Technological learning and policy alignment have contributed to China's manufacturing shift.

options.html: Advanced software and integrated supply chains now characterise many Chinese products.
options.text: Advanced software and integrated supply chains now characterise many Chinese products.

options.html: Western concern extends beyond prices to questions of long-term competitiveness.
options.text: Western concern extends beyond prices to questions of long-term competitiveness.

questions.explanationHTML:
Correct Answer: b) Chinese firms have completely abandoned cost competitiveness in favour of premium pricing.

Explanation:
Paragraph 2 explicitly states: "The emphasis has shifted from merely producing cheaper alternatives to delivering products that combine affordability with technical sophistication." Thus, Chinese firms have not abandoned affordability/cost competitiveness, making option (b) FALSE.

questions.passageHTML:
Directions : Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

For much of the late twentieth century, Chinese manufacturing was associated primarily with low-cost, low-durability goods designed to meet mass demand in price-sensitive markets. These products were often dismissed in advanced economies as functional but inferior substitutes, suitable mainly where affordability outweighed performance. Over time, however, this perception has become increasingly outdated. Chinese firms have steadily moved beyond cost-led competitiveness to invest in research, design, and systems integration, allowing them to compete in segments once dominated by Western and Japanese manufacturers.

This transformation has been driven by a deliberate alignment of industrial policy, scale advantages, and technological learning. Rather than relying solely on imitation, firms have absorbed global knowledge while adapting it to domestic conditions, producing innovations that are incremental yet cumulative. As a result, Chinese products now incorporate advanced software, data-driven optimisation, and integrated supply chains that reduce production cycles and improve reliability. The emphasis has shifted from merely producing cheaper alternatives to delivering products that combine affordability with technical sophistication.

The implications of this shift extend beyond consumer markets into strategic sectors such as renewable energy, telecommunications, and advanced manufacturing. Countries long regarded as technological leaders increasingly recognise that China is not only catching up but, in some domains, setting benchmarks. Even economies like Germany, traditionally confident in their engineering depth, express concern about the speed and coordination with which Chinese firms translate research into scalable output. This unease is not rooted solely in price competition but in the possibility that established innovation hierarchies may be reconfigured.

Western responses to this development reveal an underlying tension. On the one hand, collaboration with Chinese suppliers remains economically attractive due to efficiency gains and integrated production networks. On the other, policymakers and industries worry about dependency, standards control, and long-term competitiveness. The debate is therefore less about whether Chinese products have improved and more about how global systems should adapt to a landscape in which technological leadership is no longer geographically concentrated. Understanding this evolution requires moving beyond outdated stereotypes and acknowledging the structural capabilities that now underpin Chinese manufacturing.

questions.questionHTML:
Which of the following statements is/are supported by the passage?

A. Chinese manufacturing has evolved beyond imitation.

B. Western fears are limited to short-term price competition.

C. Technological leadership is becoming less geographically concentrated.
questions.explanationHTML:
Correct Answer: d) Both A and C

Explanation:
• Statement A is supported by Paragraph 2 ("Rather than relying solely on imitation, firms have absorbed global knowledge...").
• Statement B is contradicted by Paragraph 3 ("This unease is not rooted solely in price competition...").
• Statement C is supported by Paragraph 4 ("...a landscape in which technological leadership is no longer geographically concentrated").

questions.questionHTML:
In the given question, a word has been given and there are three ways in which the word has been used, in similar or different forms. You need to see which of the sentences has/have correctly used the highlighted word, and mark that as your answer.

Bland

I. To make the line appear less stepped, we bland the colour of the edge of the line with the colours around it.

II. Brad and Julia tramped up the stairs, each carrying a bland laden with food and cups of coffee.

III. The visuals of the movie are disappointingly mediocre, featuring bland track designs.
questions.explanationHTML:
Correct Answer: b) Only III

Explanation:
• Sentence I confuses bland with blend (to mix colours).
• Sentence II misuses bland where a noun like tray is needed.
• Sentence III correctly uses the adjective bland (uninteresting/mediocre) to describe track designs.

questions.questionHTML:
In the given question, a word has been given and there are three ways in which the word has been used, in similar or different forms. You need to see which of the sentences has/have correctly used the highlighted word, and mark that as your answer.

Lie

I. He was the most cheerful person I knew and now he lies dead in his coffin.

II. His facial expressions were the indicators of him telling a lie.

III. He was the only member of the club who didn't lie plum pudding.
questions.explanationHTML:
Correct Answer: b) Only I and II

Explanation:
• Sentence I correctly uses the verb lies (to be in a horizontal/resting state).
• Sentence II correctly uses the noun lie (an intentionally false statement).
• Sentence III erroneously uses lie instead of like ("didn't like plum pudding").

questions.questionHTML:
In the given question, a word has been given and there are three ways in which the word has been used, in similar or different forms. You need to see which of the sentences has/have correctly used the highlighted word, and mark that as your answer.

Conditions

I) The weather conditions are favourable for sailing.

II) The old car is in good driving conditions.

III) Reena conditions her hair with a conditioner.
questions.explanationHTML:
Correct Answer: e) Only I, III

Explanation:
• Sentence I correctly uses the plural noun conditions ("weather conditions").
• Sentence II is ungrammatical because the idiom for state of repair is singular: "in good driving condition".
• Sentence III correctly uses conditions as a singular verb ("Reena conditions her hair").

questions.questionHTML:
In the question below, a sentence is given with two words missing. You are given five options each containing a pair of words that can or cannot fill the blanks grammatically and/or contextually. Identify the words that are opposite in meaning to each other and make the sentence grammatically and contextually correct.

These ______ alleys eventually merge into a ______ expressway.
questions.explanationHTML:
Correct Answer: b) Narrow, broad

Explanation:
"Narrow" and "broad" are antonyms that fit both grammatically and contextually: "These narrow alleys eventually merge into a broad expressway."

In the question below, a sentence is given with two words missing. You are given five options each containing a pair of words that can or cannot fill the blanks grammatically and/or contextually. Identify the words that are opposite in meaning to each other and make the sentence grammatically and contextually correct.

The tumour seems ______, but it might turn ______ later on.
questions.explanationHTML:
Correct Answer: c) Benign, malignant

Explanation:
In medical terminology, "benign" (non-cancerous/harmless) and "malignant" (cancerous/virulent) are exact antonyms: "The tumour seems benign, but it might turn malignant later on."

questions.questionHTML:
In the question given below, a sentence is given with two blanks. Choose the correct combination of words that fit in the sentence.

From time to time ___________ the history, the title of Great has been bestowed upon a ruler who has distinguished himself, either through the splendour of his conquests _____ the value of his services to his fellowmen.
questions.explanationHTML:
Correct Answer: c) Throughout, or

Explanation:
• Blank 1 requires the preposition "throughout" (meaning all the way through history; "thorough" is an adjective).
• Blank 2 pairs with "either", requiring the correlative conjunction "or" ("either through the splendour... or the value...").

questions.questionHTML:
In the question given below, a sentence is given with two blanks. Choose the correct combination of words that fit in the sentence.

Adding journalism to my professional endeavours has __________ my communication skills, widened my range of expression, and provided me with _________ to a plethora of interesting interviews.
questions.explanationHTML:
Correct Answer: a) Refined, access

Explanation:
• Blank 1 follows "has", requiring the past participle "refined" (improved/polished).
• Blank 2 is followed by the preposition "to", requiring the noun "access" ("provided me with access to a plethora of...").

questions.questionHTML:
In the question given below, a sentence is given with two blanks. Choose the correct combination of words that fit in the sentence.

This is the _______ hit movie of the year and wins an international ______ too.
questions.explanationHTML:
Correct Answer: e) biggest, award

Explanation:
• Blank 1 follows the definite article "the", requiring the superlative adjective "biggest" ("the biggest hit movie of the year").
• Blank 2 follows "wins an international", requiring the singular countable noun "award".
